designs.summary:
Extend 513's existing (GB, GB:nhs-body, <parent code>) verdicts. A new reviewed, HIGH, members-exact cohort on a parent code P may name, as members, the holders of the child codes that ODS dates under P: RO98 sub-ICB locations by RE5, and the measured RO198 trust sites by RE6. Membership is gated structurally by the dated child map and by nhs_ods::check(P, name) over every mention name. The fold reuses the existing wet path unchanged. The child's GBNHS<C> becomes a merged identifier of the survivor, which repoint_merged_identifiers (canonical.rs:4778-4795) already writes. Only two pieces are new.
- An exact-triple arm in the nhs-body alias, armed from the ledger and gated by name. It is needed because identified mentions never reach today's name alias (canonical.rs:19208-19235), and org_of is preloaded from own identifiers only (17044-17094). A merged identifier alone routes nothing.
- A cohort scope on the unwind.

The frozen table gains a dated `parents` column (version bump) and the measured RC2 site rows, kept out of the check's rival set.

Unit 2 phase A folds the children of PPON-survivor bodies: 22 orgs, 945 of the 1,844 class-A mentions (B2M3M 600, 26A 115, D4U1Y 65, …). It holds, as `child-into-anchor`, the children of provisional-anchor bodies (13 orgs, 290 mentions), because folding a canonical row into a provisional one is the capture 300 forbids. The digit-coded parents QF7/QU9/… (8 orgs, 30 mentions) are also held; both go to a conditional identity-survivor unit. 13T is held by the name gate: its mention names mix NENC and the CSU, so no whole-org fold is right.

Typos and foreign values go through 452 verdicts plus the 453 rekey arm, not membership. Rekey works today when the correct identifier is a company number or a PPON (QHL15E → QHL survivor's PPON). It refuses GB-NHS right numbers (`unkeyed`, canonical.rs:29349; crosswalk.rs:429-433), so RF1→R1F, T6YOW→T6Y0W and the typed names (about 18 mentions) need an optional E0-owner extension. Real codes on the wrong holder (13T, RJ7, Y54/Y61/Y62, RH8C3) need mention-level rehoming.

# 519 unit 2: fold child codes into their body through 513's nhs-body verdicts (angle: extend-513) ## 0. The shape in one paragraph There is no new rule family, no new verdict scheme and no mint. A **child code** is an ODS code that ODS dates under a body's code. There are two kinds: - an RO98 sub-ICB location under an RO261 ICB (relationship RE5); - a *measured* RO198 trust site under its RO197 trust (relationship RE6). How it works: 1. The frozen table gains a dated `parents` column. 2. The nhs-body census lists the holders of every child code dated under an allowlisted code P, in any period, as holders of P. 3. A new reviewed, HIGH, members-exact `nhs-body` verdict on P may name them as members. It is a new cohort. The newest merge supersedes the applied one, because `merge_verdict_for` orders by `reviewed_at DESC` (canonical.rs:29114-29140). 4. The wet path folds them into P's standing survivor through the unchanged `nhs_body_fold` (27116-27213). 5. The child's `GBNHS` lands on the survivor as a merged identifier. `repoint_merged_identifiers` already writes it (4778-4795), so `?identifier=GBNHS` answers the survivor. Only two mechanics are new: - **(a) An exact-triple arm in the nhs-body alias.** It is armed from the ledger and gated by name. - **(b) A cohort scope on `unwind_nhs_body`.** Everything else is new fields on existing structs. ## 1. The rule: which org a child identity belongs to ### 1.1 A reviewed verdict, with derived eligibility The act is a reviewer verdict. The rule only decides who may be a member. That keeps 300's ladder: two canonical rows with different identifiers merge only by review (362) or by a shared key, and here they share no key. A child-code holder h of child code C is **eligible** as a member of body P only if every one of these structural conditions holds. No verdict overrides them. 1. **The map dates C under P.** `parents(C)` contains P for some period (RE5 for RO98, RE6 for RO198), and P is allowlisted, i.e. a 513 body. 2. **The identity shape is the child itself.** h's own identifier is exactly `GBNHS`, kind `national`, country `GB` (an identity holder). Or h is a provisional cluster bound by coded parties of a zero-only child tail (`00N`, `00P`, `00X`, `00L`): those mint nothing (the all-zero rule) and bind by name. Any other own identifier keeps 513's `minted-identity` denial (canonical.rs:26547-26550, 26575-26577). 3. **The name gate (1.3)** passes under P. 4. **No PPON.** h carries no PPON, own or merged (`child-carries-ppon`). A 469 U5 register merge keeps the register org, so folding it would orphan an altid alias target. 5. **513's other D6 denials** still apply: `generic`, `consortium`, `successor-name`, `contested`, `gone`. **Why reviewed, not derived (for example "fold into `name_icb`"):** - **13T.** It is 504 mentions under NENC's sub-ICB code. Its top names in the 513 census are "North East and North Cumbria Integrated…" **and** "NORTH OF ENGLAND COMMISSIONING SUPPORT" (`../513-nhs/u5/plan-2279-dry-final.json`, `off_allowlist`). Its mentions are two bodies, so any whole-org fold is wrong, and the head name decides nothing. - **Small mass.** Review covers at most about 52 + 25 child holders plus a handful of `00X` clusters: one U3-style batch. - **Canonical rows.** These are canonical rows. 513 D2 only let provisional clusters fold into a canonical row. ### 1.2 Dated parents `parents(C)` is a list of `(parent, rel, from, to)` (Operational dates, the ones unit 1 read). **The name chooses among the dated parents, never "today's parent".** 26A is QMM until 2026-03-31 and T6Y0W after, but its notices are Norfolk and Waveney (QMM). A child dated under two allowlisted parents is listed under both. D4U1Y is under QNQ until 2026-03-31, then QRL. The existing `contested` rule (canonical.rs:26439-26447) denies it if both verdicts name it. **No date fence on the fold**, as in 513 ("legally-ended codes have no date fence"). Post-switch mentions that still carry the old body's name fold with it. Post-switch mentions that carry the new body's name are caught by the name gate (1.3), at fold time and at bind time. The census still reports, per child holder, its mentions inside and outside P's period (`notices.published_at`, which `nhs_org_facts` already reads, 7698), so a reader sees the exposure. ### 1.3 The name gate `nhs_ods::check(P, name)` (nhs_ods.rs:275-327) must answer `admitted` for: - the holder's head name, and - **every distinct mention name** the census reads for it (child holders are small, so the read is complete; a capped read denies, `child-names-unread`). The denials are `child-name` (head) and `child-name-mixed` (any mention name, with the failing names listed). A `tie` refuses. This is stricter than 513's D3, where the check is a flag a HIGH verdict can override. Here it is structural, because the members are canonical rows and the ODS name is the only evidence that ties a sub-ICB location's org to the body. The check already treats every table row as a rival, including the RO98 row itself ("NHS COVENTRY AND WARWICKSHIRE ICB - B2M3M" carries the code token, so the parent wins) and the 2026 five-character ICBs. So `check(QMM, "NHS Norfolk and Suffolk ICB")` refuses with `better{T6Y0W}`, and `check(QHM, "North of England Commissioning Support")` refuses with `role`. The same check gates the bind (3.5), so prevention is never looser than the verified merge (the 310/448 rule). ### 1.4 What unit 2 folds and what it holds The partition below comes from `sub-icb.json` (`name_icb`, overlap ≥ 0.5) and the U5 wet plans' `folded[].target`. | class | parent survivor | orgs / mentions | unit 2 | |---|---|---|---| | A1 | PPON org: QWU QMM QNQ QHL QJK QMJ QUA QRL QHM QWO QOC QVV QOQ QPM QGH QXU | **22 / 945** (B2M3M 600, 26A 115, D4U1Y 65, 15E 46, 15N 31, 93C 23, …) | **fold** (phase A) | | A2 | provisional anchor: QOX QKS QWE QSL QKK QMF QHG QUE QNC QNX QYG | 13 / 290 (92G 80, 72Q 47, 91Q 41, …) | hold `child-into-anchor`; U6 | | A3 | digit-coded parent, an identity org not on the allowlist: QF7 QU9 QK1 QE1 QH8 QJ2 QM7 | 8 / 30 | hold (`child_unanchored`); U6 | | rest | 13T (504, mixed names); 15C (31, QUY still held in 513 U6); 15A and W2U3Z (five-character 2026 parents); 03K, 14J, 14N (no RO261 parent); 03Q, 04Y (another body's name) | 9 / 579 | not members; listed | **Why hold A2:** - With no PPON member, `nhs_body_survivor` takes the largest cluster as a provisional anchor (6634-6642). Folding canonical `GBNHS92G` into a provisional row is the canonical→provisional capture 300/E3 forbids. - The fix is the "identity survivor" (U6), the only further concept. It needs three pieces: - a survivor tier, so an identity member beats an anchor; - an anchor-chain follow in `nhs_body_target_org` (6762-6775), so the pre-flip 513 rows still resolve; - a `GBNHS

` hand-back in the scoped unwind. **Trust sites (class B, 25 orgs / 36 mentions)** go through the same rule. A site-code org named as its trust passes `check(trust, name)` and is eligible. A site-named org ("Leighton Hospital") fails and stays a separate buying point, which keeps 513's "hosted sites stay separate". Sites under PPON-survivor trusts (RBT, RCU) fold in phase A. Sites under anchors (RJN71) or under digit-coded trusts (RJ1, RH8) are held like A2 and A3. ## 2. Data ### 2.1 The table `crates/ingest/sdk/nhs-ods.tsv` gains a **10th column `parents`**. - **Format:** `;`-separated `CODE:REL:FROM:TO`, for example `QMM:RE5:2019-10-23:2026-03-31;T6Y0W:RE5:2026-04-01:`. An empty TO means open. - **RO98 rows:** filled for all 344 (Active and Inactive), from ORD `Rels.Rel` with `id == RE5` and target primary role RO261. - **New RC2 rows, primary role RO198:** only the measured site codes (unit 1's class B list, about 25), as `MEASURED_RO172` does for DQF. Each has `allow 0` and RE6 parents. - **Empty for every other row.** The allow, predecessor, successor and legal_end columns do not change. - **Version:** `ods-2026-10-1x` (generation date). The header adds `# parents:` and `# rows: … plus RO198 sites for the measured codes only` lines. ### 2.2 The generator `.scratch/tender-db/513-nhs/u1-table/gen_nhs_ods_table.py` (one generator, one table): - Fetch `org_record(code)` for every RO98 row and every `MEASURED_RO198` code. It is cached as `raw/org_.json`. The first run seeds raw/ from `../../519-nhs-digit-codes/ods-table-codes/` (66 records) and `../../519-nhs-digit-codes/ods/` (the site records), as it already seeds from the legacy caches. - Parse RE5 and RE6 into `parents`. - Exit non-zero if: - a child's RE5 target is missing from the table; - a site's RE6 target is not RO197; - two Active RE5 periods overlap. - Print the count of children per allowlisted parent and the RO98 codes with no RO261 parent (03K, 14J, 14N). - `--offline` still rebuilds byte for byte. ### 2.3 nhs_ods.rs and the store types - **`parse`** reads ten fields (nhs_ods.rs:380-382 destructures nine and panics otherwise). - **`Org`** gains `parents: Vec, to: Option<&str> }>`. - **New `children(code) -> &[&'static Org]`**: the reverse index, built once in `Table`. - **`check`** skips rows with `rc1 == false` as rivals (the loop at 298-307). There are no RC2 rows today, so this changes nothing for 513, and the `nhs_ods_adjudication_tally` harness must re-measure 233/235 and 116/116 exactly. - **`census_code`** (332-343) fills `NhsOdsCode.parents`. - **New `census_children`.** - **Store:** - `NhsOdsCode` (canonical.rs:5833-5846) gains `parents: Vec`; - `NhsBodyArgs` (5904-5934) gains `children: fn(&str) -> Vec`; - the supervisor wires it at supervisor.rs:10461-10476. ### 2.4 What the census lists for child codes The census is `plan_nhs_bodies_on`, with a new **child pass** after step 2 (26337-26353), boxed (CLAUDE.md stack rule). **Child holders of each allowlisted P.** For each child C of P (any period): - identity holders: one seek per child literal on the identity index, `identifier = 'GBNHS'` (the triple shape is checked); - the coded holders the harvest already bound for tail C, for three-character children. Today they go to `off_allowlist` (26761-26798, which already shows 13T, 26A, 92G and 00P with their holders). These join P's `holder_ids` (the live set `reviewed_holders` must equal) and `holder_of`. **New `NhsBodyCode.children: Vec`**, with fields: - `code`, `role`, `ods_name`; - `periods_here` (the periods under P) and `other_parents` (code, from, to); - `holder_ids`, `coded_parties`. **New per-holder fields** on `NhsBodyHolder` (5953-6020): - `child_of: Option<&str>`; - `child_names: [{name_norm, n, in_period, out_of_period, check_here, check_other_parents[]}]`; - denials: `child-name`, `child-name-mixed`, `child-names-unread`, `child-carries-ppon`, `child-triple-shape`. `via` must be recomputed from four flags (party, later, ppon, child). Today `(false, false, _)` reads "ppon" (26605-26613), which would mislabel a child-only holder. **Report-level:** - `child_codes_seen`, `child_holders`, `child_mentions`, `child_denied{reason}`; - `child_unanchored`: children whose every dated parent is off the allowlist (A3 and the five-character parents), with their holders; - `child_no_parent`. **Status changes** (26659-26716): - The D4 owned-elsewhere test (26692-26710) skips identity child members, because their name key is never armed (3.5). Zero-only cluster members keep it. - New status `child-into-anchor`: the verdict names a child member and the survivor `nhs_body_survivor` would pick is not a PPON target. Such a verdict is never admitted. ## 3. Merge mechanics ### 3.1 The verdict One verdict lineage per body is the reason this is not a separate rule: - The key stays `(GB, GB:nhs-body, P)`, so `MergeVerdict::validate`'s three-character key check (canonical.rs:8446-8452) is untouched. - Members are {P's live survivor} ∪ the child members (∪ any newly read SAME clusters). - `reviewed_holders` = P's live holder set as 2.4 widens it: code holders ∪ PPON holders ∪, for every child dated under P, its identity holders and coded holders. Members-exact keeps its meaning over a wider set, and a newcomer child holder makes the verdict `stale`. - A body not yet applied (QUY) takes its child (15C) in the same verdict. **Why not a child-keyed or separate rule:** - It would duplicate U2-U4. - It would split one body's members-exact set across two keys. - It would collide in the alias. A key that two **codes'** rows claim is poisoned (17544-17548), so a zero-only child cluster's name key ("nhs north east and north cumbria integrated care board" under 00P) would poison QHM's own loser key. ### 3.2 The fold `merge_nhs_bodies` and `nhs_body_fold` do not change except as follows: - `nhs_body_survivor` (6608-6643) excludes identity members from the anchor tier, so they never become a provisional anchor. A wet hold `child-into-anchor` backs up the census status. - `loser-ppon-unaliased` (27040-27048) is unchanged. - For each loser, `repoint_org_references` (27175) moves mentions, parties, bid-parties, winners and names, and writes the loser's own literal as a merged identifier (4778-4795, rule `nhs-body`). The row is deleted, the ledger row and `organization removed` are written. - The fold also records `GBNHS` for a zero-only child code it folded (`record_alias_identifier_as`, 4929), so `?identifier=GBNHS00P` answers the survivor too. - The verdict stamp (27196-27206) stamps the new cohort. ### 3.3 The loser's GBNHS - The row goes, and its literal stays findable as `organization_merged_identifiers(GBNHS, national, GB, keep, loser, 'nhs-body')`. `?identifier=GBNHS` answers the survivor, which is S3's check. - A from-archive rebuild empties that table (460 D5). The triple arm re-records it on each bind, as the name alias re-records `GBNHS` (17774-17789). ### 3.4 The ledger evidence `nhs_body_ledger_evidence` (6528-6577) writes, for an identity loser: - `loser_kind: "identity"` (today `ppon|name`, 6567); - `loser_id: "GBNHS"`; - a new `loser_identifier_kind`; - `loser_name` and `loser_names` (for the reader); - `loser_name_norm: ""` and `loser_name_norms: []`; - new `child_code`, `child_rel` and `child_periods`. The empty name keys are deliberate. The alias's name map skips rows without `loser_name_norm` (17496-17498), the unwind's key set drops empty norms (27389-27398), and S4's name probe needs one (26893). So **every existing name path ignores identity rows with no code change**, and only the triple paths read them. A child's mentions are all identified: identifier-less mentions bind only `identifier IS NULL` rows. So nothing is lost by not arming its name. Zero-only child clusters are ordinary `name` losers. ### 3.5 The alias: re-binding future child-coded mentions **Today a merged identifier routes nothing:** - `org_of` is preloaded from `organizations.identifier` only (17044-17094). - The resolver reads `organization_merged_identifiers` only for issue 470's folded lookalikes (18720-18737). - The nhs-body alias is asked only in the identifier-less branch (19208-19235). So after the fold, the next `GB-NHS-B2M3M` mention misses `org_of`, the rekey map, the canon key (GB-NHS keys nothing, crosswalk.rs:429-433), the anchor path and the altid alias, and **mints** `GBNHSB2M3M` again (19133-19174). **The new arm:** - **Arming.** `NHS_BODY_ALIAS_LEDGER_SQL` (6270-6276) adds `$.loser_kind`, `$.loser_id` and `$.loser_identifier_kind`. `arm_nhs_body_alias_on` (17487-17625) puts identity rows into a new `NhsBodyAlias.triples: HashMap<(Option, String, String), NhsBodyKey>`, keyed by `(GB, national, GBNHS)` with the row's code (P), target and `keep_name`. The arming rules are the same as for name keys: - `keep` verdicts drop rows; - a triple two codes claim is poisoned; - the newest row wins; - anchor chains followed. A triple that a `wrong` or unapplied `related` verdict names (`withheld_triples`) is armed but refuses. - **The name check** arrives through `AltIdAliasRules` (8012-8034) as `nhs_check: Option NhsNameCheck>`, set to `Some(nhs_ods::census_check)` in `project::altid_alias_rules` (project.rs:2053-2065). Three test literals change too. `arm_altid_alias` passes it on. With `None`, the triple map is not armed, and that is logged. - **The bind** runs at the head of `resolve_one_mention`'s identified branch, **before** `org_of.get` (18633-18635), and only for an armed triple. Steps: 1. Answer `check(P, m.name)`, memoized per (P, name_norm). 2. If admitted, find or mint the body's target with the code factored out of `nhs_body_alias_bind`'s target match (17671-17768): exact PPON triple, rekey, canon key, altid follow, else mint under `keep_name`. 3. Record `GBNHS

` and the mention's own `GBNHS` on it, once per run. 4. Never cache the result in `org_of`. It is a name-conditional bind (the 318/448 rule). Refused, withheld or shared: the mention falls through **unchanged** to `org_of` or the mint, so a mis-publisher (a CSU under a sub-ICB code, a post-merger body under a moved child) stands on its own `GBNHS` row. The arm must precede `org_of`. Otherwise the first refused mention's mint would claim the triple, and every later correctly named mention would bind the stray by exact triple. Boxed like 19215. - **Counts** on `NhsBodyAliasCounts` (6464-6489): `triples`, `triple_asked`, `triple_bound`, `triple_minted`, `triple_refused_name`, `triple_refused_withheld`, `triple_standing` (a standing row carries an armed triple). There is a new `[issue 519]` diag line on every armed fold. ### 3.6 The unwind `unwind_nhs_body` (27244-27650) mostly works already: - **Identity losers already dissolve.** Each ledger `loser_id` is a literal (27399). A survivor mention whose raw normalises to it goes to `Dest::Identity`: the standing row, or a minted one (27421-27425, 27514-27520). The loser redirects there (27585-27604), and its literal is dropped off the survivor (27612-27619). Additions: 1. **`NhsBodyUnwindArgs.cohort: Option<&str>`.** It filters rows by `$.cohort`. The supervisor's `nhs-body-unwind` request takes `cohort` (supervisor.rs:1574-1577; the Spec variant at 426 gains a field, so no new `run_spec` arm). 2. **When scoped and rows of the code remain outside the scope** (513's own fold), do not drop `GBNHS

` (today it is dropped unconditionally, 27606-27611). 3. **Also drop alias-recorded `GBNHS`** (rule `nhs-body`, `loser = org_id`) for each identity literal. Survivors must still agree (27366-27375). The one-member path (27290-27333) is untouched. ### 3.7 S4 In `nhs_body_ledger_listing` (26824-26936), the literal-regrown probe (26913-26928, labelled "ppon" today) labels identity rows by kind: - `identity` (halt) when the regrown row's head name or any mention name passes `check(P)`. The alias should have bound it. - `identity-stray` (listed, no halt) otherwise: a different publisher under the child code. This needs `args.check` passed in. ## 4. Rekey **refuses** today (`unkeyed`, 29349-29352; GB-NHS keys nothing, crosswalk.rs:429-433). Optional U7: a merge-only E0 owner when the right literal is exactly one org's own (GB, national) identifier, behind the same name gates. | | concatenated pharmacy codes, CQC and OCDS ids, junk | most of F/E's rest | none | 452 `wrong` without a correction: withheld status only; the org stays (its exact triple still binds, 17028-17037). | | real ODS codes on the wrong holder: 13T, RJ7 (Kingston under St George's code), Y54/Y61/Y62, RH8C3 | ~520 | — | **not org-level.** The code is real and its org mixes two bodies' mentions, so a fold or rekey would mis-file one of them. Mention-level rehoming (317 verdicts), or leave. | **Why not fold typos as members:** the dated map is the eligibility domain, and a typo is not in it. Admitting typos would need a second, fuzzy relation (edit distance), the kind 513 kept to the unique O/0 fold. Only QHL15E's target is a 513 body, and the PPON correction covers it without new code. ## 5. Dry plan, stop rules, canary **The dry plan** is the same job, `match-org-identifiers {"rule":"nhs-body"}` → `nhs-body-plan`. On top of today's report it carries: - per code: `children[]`; - per child holder: `child_names` with in- and out-of-period counts and checks, plus the child denials; - `child_unanchored` and `child_no_parent`; - the status `child-into-anchor`; - `nhs_body_regrown` kinds `identity` and `identity-stray`. **Stop rules:** - **S0.** No verdict for a parent with an unread child holder. `reviewed_holders` equals the live widened set. 0 child members with any child denial. - **S1.** - Reviewer and challenger agree HIGH on every child member. - 0 members whose names are `better` or `tie` under any rival. - 13T, 03Q and 04Y are never members. - Halt if more than 2 of the 22 phase-A holders fail the strict all-names gate on spelling noise alone (then decide 8-M1). - **S2.** Parity max(2%, 5) (existing, 26975-26991). - **S3 (capped read).** For each folded child: - the loser answers 308; - `?identifier=GBNHS` answers exactly the survivor, and no row carries `GBNHS` as its own identifier; - `?identifier=GBNHS

The design is a new, narrow merge arm, `nhs-child` (scheme `GB:nhs-child`, ledger rule `nhs-child`). It folds the canonical GBNHS<child> identity org of a sub-ICB location, a trust site, or a reviewed alias of a body's code into the live survivor of its parent's body. It runs under a reviewed, members-exact verdict with a hard ODS name gate, and nothing of 513 changes: its verdict semantics, planner, survivor rule, table and VERSION all stay as they are.

The parent is the dated ODS parent that every one of the holder's names fits (`child_check`). It does not have to be today's parent, and a tie holds the org. Dates are census evidence only, as in 513.

The data is a separate frozen `sdk/nhs-ods-children.tsv` with dated RE5/RE6 rows and its own version. 513's table, its `check` rivals and `ods_version` stay byte-identical.

**How the fold works.**
- Each fold calls `repoint_org_references(keep, loser, "nhs-child")`, which leaves GBNHS<child> on the survivor as a merged identifier (canonical.rs:4744/4783). So `?identifier=` answers the survivor and the loser answers 308.
- That merged identifier does not route the resolver: `org_of` is preloaded from `organizations` only (17046), and GB-NHS keys nothing (crosswalk.rs:748-749). So the arm adds an identity-keyed alias, armed from the ledger and consulted at the head of the identified branch (before 18634) for armed child triples only. It binds a mention only when the mention's name passes the gate.
- A scoped unwind ships with it, and `unwind_nhs_body` gains a guard. Without the guard, child mentions would stay on a dissolved survivor (27424).

**Typos and foreign values.** NHS-body typos (RF1, T6YOW, QHL15E, the typed RW4) fold as reviewed alias members. The alternative of 452 verdicts plus the rekey arm fails here: the rekey arm counts every GB-NHS correct_identifier as `unkeyed` (29343-29350) and cannot reach letter-only bodies. Foreign-scheme values (Companies House numbers, PPONs) use 452 + rekey unchanged, and junk is only withheld.

**Cohorts and what to measure first.**
- Cohort 1 folds into canonical survivors only: 30 sub-ICB orgs (975 mentions), 13T into 0AR's PPON body (504) and 4 typos — 35 orgs, about 1,495 mentions.
- Cohort 2 is the 13 orgs (290 mentions) whose parent body is provisional. It needs a written 300 §10 amendment first.
- Measure first: every holder's mention names and dates against `child_check`, especially across the 2026-04 mergers. Also refetch 03K: unit 1's 'no parent' for it was a failed fetch (http 000).

The rule: which org a child identity belongs to ### 1.1 Reviewed verdict, derived proposal, derived prevention **The fold is reviewed.** It needs one verdict per child code, keyed (`GB`, `GB:nhs-child`, ``). The planner derives a proposal for each code, and the reviewer confirms it (`merge`, HIGH) or holds it (`keep`). The structural gates in 1.3–1.5 are hard: a verdict can only confirm what they admit, never override them. Why review rather than a derived rule: - Members-exact protects against drift. The fixes: an NHS-aware rekey key, owners found through the `nhs-body` merged identifiers, a move only onto a digit-bearing code, five derived gates (child map, B4 name check, moved parent, no body, not an organisation), a `rekey-nhs` ledger rule whose targets are keyed by identity, and a merged `GBNHS<child>` for confirmed children. The resolver gets a tiered alias (name-blind only while the target is the code's current parent) and a scoped unwind. The child map goes in a sibling TSV, so 513's check rivals and its 233/235 tally stay byte-identical. The angle's hard limit: one verdict per triple cannot route a code that two bodies publish (moved children after 2026-04, 13T if NENC uses it), so measure that exposure (M1/M4) first.

**Mechanics (verified).**
- Merged identifiers route nothing in the resolver. org_of is preloaded from organizations.identifier only, the identified branch probes org_of first (canonical.rs:18633), and merged_hit applies only to O/0-folded keys (18720).

- extend-513 and separate-arm both put it first, gate it by name and never cache it.
- identifier-verdicts consults its fallback only on a miss, and binds its 'open' tier name-blind and cached. That steers future mis-publishers into the ICB and lets a stray carrier mix both bodies.
